items.summary: A personal AI agent is software that acts for one person, using their accounts, data and payment details to complete tasks such as booking, buying and emailing.

items.title: Referrer
items.summary: A referrer is the address of the page a visitor came from, which browsers pass in the HTTP Referer header and analytics tools read to label each traffic source.

items.title: Referrer policy
items.summary: Referrer policy is the browser rule deciding how much of a page's URL is sent in the Referer header, shaping attribution, privacy leaks and ad tech page data.

items.title: Direct traffic
items.summary: Direct traffic is the analytics channel for visits that arrive with no referrer and no campaign tag, a catch-all for typed URLs, apps, email and lost data.

items.title: Server logs
items.summary: Server logs are the files a web server writes for every request it handles, recording IP, time, URL, status and user agent. They show what really hit a site.

items.title: Referral exclusion
items.summary: Referral exclusion is an analytics setting that stops listed domains, such as payment gateways or a site's own pages, from claiming credit as traffic sources.

items.title: Core update

items.summary: A paywall is a barrier that withholds digital content until a reader pays, usually by subscription. Hard, metered, freemium and dynamic versions all differ.

items.title: Similarweb

items.title: Unique visitors
items.summary: Unique visitors are the distinct people or browsers that reach a website in a set period, counted once however often they return, the basis of audience claims.

Tested across five public security benchmarks, AAD successfully caught 87% of harmful instructions carried out by agents without adding runtime latency. Developers can integrate AAD alongside semantic governance and strict tool limits as part of a defense-in-depth strategy to secure agentic applications.

items.summary: Developers can now build applications powered by Google Maps Platform directly within Google AI Studio by prompting Gemini with real-world geospatial concepts. The integration eliminates traditional configuration hurdles by providing one-click demo keys that generate instantly without requiring Cloud Console redirects or credit cards. This setup grants developers immediate access to core APIs—including Maps, Places, and Routes—supported by daily sandbox quotas for seamless prototyping.

items.summary: LiteRT in Google Play services now offers GPU inference powered by ML Drift, delivering about 1.4x faster performance alongside the new CompiledModel API. Switching from bundled binaries reduces app size by approximately 8 MB while enabling seamless, automatic runtime updates across billions of devices. Developers can easily adopt these updates by updating their dependencies and utilizing the new Android Studio LiteRT skill for automated migration.

Additionally, it demonstrates how platform teams can author custom extensions to enforce policies such as automated software bill of materials (SBOM) scans during deployment.
